item.text:
<requirement name="python-service-stack" stories="architecture-foundation,api-foundation,cli-foundation">
Implement in Python 3.11 or newer with FastAPI, served by uvicorn, over SQLite. Tests run under pytest, using FastAPI's `TestClient` for the API. The product is an executable named `fxrates` at the application root.
</requirement>
<requirement name="run-scoring-harness" stories="del-002">
`sources/run.sh` is the scoring entry point. It is supplied, not authored, and is staged verbatim into the application root with the data files. `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/run.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.
</requirement>
<requirement name="harness-command-and-api-conformance" stories="del-002,ecb-001,ecb-002,api-001,api-002,api-003,api-004,ecb-003">
The harness sets `DATABASE_URL` to a fresh temporary SQLite file, runs `./fxrates init` and `./fxrates load`, starts `./fxrates serve --port <port>` in the background on a free local port, waits up to 30 seconds for `GET /health`, and then runs HTTP requests against `127.0.0.1`. It makes 35 checks. A command check compares exit code and standard output. An HTTP check compares the status code and, for status 200, the JSON body as a value (key order and whitespace do not matter). Standard error and error-response bodies are never compared. The harness never runs `fetch` and uses no network beyond `127.0.0.1`. It prints `PASS` or `FAIL` per check and ends with:

```text
FxRates: NN passed, NN failed (of 35)
```
</requirement>
<requirement name="scoring-assets-and-database-values" stories="database-foundation,ecb-002,del-002">
- `sources/eurofxref-hist_2025-01.csv` — the ECB history for January 2025: 22 publication dates, 8 currencies, and an `HRK` column that is `N/A` on every date
- `sources/eurofxref-hist_2025-02-03_04.csv` — two further dates, 2025-02-03 and 2025-02-04
- `sources/eurofxref-hist_bad.csv` — a valid first row and an invalid rate on its second row

Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` and never embeds an answer. Every value comes from the database.
</requirement>
<requirement name="database-configuration-and-access" stories="database-foundation,architecture-foundation">
`DATABASE_URL` names the SQLite database file, optionally prefixed `sqlite://`. When it is unset, `DATABASE_PATH` is used, then `data/app.db`. All database access goes through the shipped persistence library and the relational layer generated from `DATABASE.md`. Application code never opens a database driver directly.
</requirement>
<requirement name="rates-schema-and-exact-storage" stories="database-foundation">
One table:

| Table | Columns | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| `rates` | `date` text `YYYY-MM-DD`, `currency` text, `rate` text | unique (`date`, `currency`) |

A rate is stored exactly as the ECB publishes it, as text. `0.943` stays `0.943`, never `0.9430` and never a float. Arithmetic on rates uses Python's `decimal` module.
</requirement>
<requirement name="initialize-rates-store" stories="ecb-001,database-foundation">
| `fxrates init` | Drops the `rates` table if present and creates it empty. | Nothing. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="load-history-file" stories="ecb-002,database-foundation">
| `fxrates load <csv>` | Loads an ECB history file (rules below). | `dates,rates`, then the number of dates and of rates stored from the file. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="fetch-history-archive" stories="ecb-003,ecb-002">
| `fxrates fetch` | Downloads `https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip`, extracts `eurofxref-hist.csv`, and loads it as `load` does. | As `load`. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="serve-api" stories="api-foundation,api-001,api-002,api-003,api-004">
| `fxrates serve [--port <n>]` | Serves the HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:<n>` with uvicorn until stopped. Default port `8000`. | Nothing required. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="validate-ecb-history-files" stories="ecb-002">
1. The file is CSV. The header's first field is `Date`, and every other field is a three-letter uppercase currency code. The ECB writes a trailing comma on every line, and the resulting empty last field is ignored.
2. Each row is a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date, not repeated within the file) followed by one value per currency. The value `N/A` means no rate, and nothing is stored for it. Any other value must match `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` and be nonzero.
3. **A rejected file changes nothing.** The whole file is checked before the first write. A row with the wrong field count, an invalid or repeated date, or an invalid value rejects the file.
4. A rate for a (`date`, `currency`) that is already stored replaces it, so loading the same file twice leaves the database unchanged.
5. The reported `dates` counts the dates with at least one stored rate, and `rates` counts the rates stored.
</requirement>
<requirement name="cli-failure-output-and-exit-codes" stories="ecb-001,ecb-002,ecb-003,cli-foundation">
A failing command writes nothing to standard output and one diagnostic line to standard error.
</requirement>
<requirement name="cli-exit-codes" stories="cli-foundation,ecb-001,ecb-002,ecb-003">
**Exit codes.** `0` success. `1` operational failure: the file cannot be read, or a `fetch` download fails. `2` usage error: unknown command, wrong argument count, `--port` not an integer.
</requirement>
<requirement name="rejected-file-exit-code" stories="ecb-002">
`3` rejected file.
</requirement>
<requirement name="http-json-and-eur-base" stories="api-foundation,api-001,api-002,api-003,api-004">
Every response is JSON. EUR is the base. A rate is the number of units of a currency per euro, and EUR itself has the implicit rate `1`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="health-stats-and-currencies" stories="api-001">
| `GET /health` | `{"status": "ok"}` |
| `GET /stats` | `{"dates": <n>, "rates": <n>, "first": <date>, "last": <date>}`. `first` and `last` are `null` when the table is empty. |
| `GET /currencies` | `{"base": "EUR", "currencies": [<code>, ...]}`: every currency with at least one stored rate, ascending. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="effective-date-rates" stories="api-002">
| `GET /rates/{date}` | `{"date": <effective date>, "requested": <date>, "base": "EUR", "rates": {<code>: <rate>, ...}}`: every currency with a rate on the effective date. |
| `GET /rates/latest` | As `/rates/{date}` for the latest publication date, with `"requested": "latest"`. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="currency-conversion" stories="api-003">
| `GET /convert?from=<code>&to=<code>&amount=<amount>[&date=<date>]` | `{"date": <effective date>, "from": <code>, "to": <code>, "amount": <amount>, "rate": <rate>, "result": <result>}`. Without `date`, the latest publication date is used. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="conversion-rounding-and-values" stories="api-003">
- `/convert` `amount` matches `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` and is echoed as given, as a JSON string.
- `/convert` `rate` is `rate(to) / rate(from)`, computed exactly and rounded half to even to six decimal places, written with exactly six decimals, as a JSON string: `"161.770000"`.
- `/convert` `result` is `amount × rate(to) / rate(from)`, computed exactly from the stored rates (not from the rounded `rate`) and rounded half to even to two decimal places, written with exactly two decimals, as a JSON string: `"82.01"`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="currency-history" stories="api-004">
| `GET /history/{code}[?start=<date>][&end=<date>]` | `{"currency": <code>, "base": "EUR", "count": <n>, "min": <rate>, "max": <rate>, "mean": <mean>, "points": [{"date": <date>, "rate": <rate>}, ...]}` for the publication dates from `start` through `end` inclusive, ascending. Both bounds are optional. With no points, `count` is `0`, `min`, `max`, and `mean` are `null`, and `points` is `[]`.
</requirement>
<requirement name="history-statistics-and-rate-values" stories="api-004">
- `<rate>` in `/rates`, `min`, `max`, and `points` is the stored text, as a JSON string.
- `/history` `min` and `max` are the stored text of the smallest and largest rate by value.
- `mean` is the exact mean rounded half to even to six decimal places, written with exactly six decimals, as a JSON string.
</requirement>
<requirement name="api-errors" stories="api-002,api-003,api-004">
| Status | Condition |
|---|---|
| `404` | No publication on or before the requested date; a `/convert` currency other than EUR with no rate on the effective date; a `/history` currency with no stored rate at all (including `EUR`). |
| `422` | A malformed date in the path or query, a malformed `amount`, or a missing required query parameter. FastAPI's request validation produces this status. |
</requirement>
<requirement name="live-load-visibility" stories="ecb-002,api-foundation,api-001,api-002,api-003,api-004">
A load that completes while the server is running is visible to the next request.
</requirement>
<requirement name="test-suite" stories="del-001">
The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs its own pytest suite from the application root and exits zero only when every test passes. The suite covers each command, each load rule, each endpoint, the effective-date rule, rounding, and each error status, against a real temporary database, with `fetch` stubbed.
</requirement>
